headline: A Reuters column argues that five market measures show US shares and bonds are stretched, with tech and AI making up more than 40% of the S&P 500.
score_reason: Keeps the pool score: an opinion column using real market data, not a news event.
importance_line: Anyone holding US index funds is heavily exposed to tech and AI shares, but the column is opinion, says the rally could continue, and does not predict when or whether a fall will come.
summary: In a Reuters commentary, columnist McGeever argues that US shares and bonds look stretched, noting that tech and AI stocks now make up over 40% of the S&P 500's market value, more than at the dotcom peak in 2000. The column also points to the lowest equity risk premium (the extra return stocks offer over safe bonds) in 24 years and the highest 30-year inflation-protected Treasury yield since 2002, while adding that strong AI profits could keep the rally going.
notes: Reuters page blocked (401); text read on Livemint, which states it came from the Reuters automated feed unmodified. It is an opinion column; the charts themselves were not visible.
